card_quote: Default answer to 'would you buy this as a gift' is no. I think novelty books end up unread on a shelf, and I want the gift done in five minutes and not to be embarrassing.
how_read: Kitchen counter, fifteen minutes. Read the How to play page, did the first four or five questions properly, then skimmed the rest of Round 1 on the answer pages. Didn't keep score. It's not a book I'd sit down with.

w1_friction.note: So AI wrote it and AI drew it. Okay. Why am I paying for it then.
w1_friction.quote: The illustrations were made with AI image tools.
Her cat, Hearsay, believes every word.

w1_friction.note: Four paragraphs on a bath. I just wanted yes or no and one line.
w1_friction.quote: how a writer two centuries later could know

w1_friction.note: I said folklore for the apple and now it's TRUE for the apple. Which is it.
w1_friction.quote: Only the apple hitting his head was added afterward.

w1_friction.note: A page to tell me a formula isn't in a paper.
w1_friction.quote: That is not the compact formula now known everywhere.

w1_friction.quote: Who first said it, and in what words, is not settled.

w1_best.why: Blood, toil, tears and sweat. One line, I could say it at work.
Moore and the 18 months, I actually get that one from my job.
Einstein's Nobel wasn't for relativity. Good bar fact.
Looking for E = mc2 in the paper and it isn't there. Short and kind of funny.
Apple on the head. Everyone's heard it so it works.

w1_flat.why: Ramps and water clocks. I stopped reading.
Same apple as the last page with the opposite answer. Annoying.
Bath, crown, Latin guy. Heard it, don't care.

w1_review.headline: Smart, but it's homework
w1_review.body: It's a nice idea but every answer is a wall of text when I just wanted the fact. I did ten questions in about fifteen minutes and was done. For a Secret Santa I'd get a gift card or a bottle of something. Bottom line: fine for someone who loves trivia, not for me to give a colleague.

w2_review_first: It's fine. The kind of thing you leave in the bathroom. If a friend asked I'd say sure it's clever, but for a gift I'd rather give a gift card.

w2_lost.why: First answer page and already four paragraphs, so I started skimming.
Einstein paper, too many words to say a simple thing.
Disputed one with a rocket sled and Air Force project. Lost me.

w2_read_aloud.why: Short, the four items thing lands instantly.
Most people guess relativity, so I get to be right.
People in tech say 18 months all the time, easy to correct them.
A familiar story with a twist, works at a table.
Tell them to go look for the formula in the paper. Makes people argue.

w2_cut.why: Disputed and tangled, no clean line.
School geometry, no one wants that at a party.
Contradicts the page before it, feels like a trick.
Everyone's heard Eureka, and the answer is two pages of Latin names.

w2_book2: If it's the same thing again with long answer pages. I probably wouldn't buy book one, never mind a second.
